preregistration_note: Written and committed before any experiment code was executed. Thresholds below must not be edited after results exist; any change must be logged as a deviation in STATUS.md.
question: When only the time grid of the same physical input path changes, which parts of a selective diagonal SSM's output change are grid artifacts, and does a simple time-handling fix (Delta scaled by physical dt + exact ZOH input matrix + time-weighted readout) remove them?
scope_limits: Toy only: scalar input channel, N diagonal stable modes, fixed random parameters, no training.
No claim about real Mamba/S4/S5 implementations is licensed by this run.
No train/dev/test split is needed because nothing is fitted; the independent evaluation unit is one seed = (one parameter draw, one input path draw).

budget.on_budget_exceeded: abort remaining experiments; mark them NOT_RUN(TIMEOUT) in results; do not report partial aggregates as complete

units.unit_definition: seed -> (lambda_n, gate w/beta, B(u), C(u), input path u(t)); grid variants of the same seed are NOT independent samples
units.aggregation: report per-unit values; aggregate as median / max / min / fraction-meeting-threshold across the 32 units

model.gate: g(u) = softplus(w*u + beta), w ~ U(-1.5, 1.5), beta ~ U(-0.5, 0.5); one gate shared across the N modes
model.continuous_time_model: dh/dt = g(u(t)) * (lambda * h + B(u(t)) * u(t)),  y(t) = Re(sum_n C_n(u(t)) h_n(t))
model.hold_convention: right-endpoint hold (Mamba/S5 recurrence convention): step k uses u_k = u(t_k) and dt_k = t_k - t_{k-1}

variants.zoh_dt: Delta = dt*g(u); Abar = exp(Delta*lambda); Bbar = expm1(Delta*lambda)/lambda * B(u)   [exact ZOH, correct dt]
variants.eulerB_dt: Delta = dt*g(u); Abar = exp(Delta*lambda); Bbar = Delta*B(u)   [correct dt, Mamba-style simplified B]
variants.bilinear_dt: Delta = dt*g(u); Abar = (1+Delta*lambda/2)/(1-Delta*lambda/2); Bbar = Delta/(1-Delta*lambda/2)*B(u)   [correct dt, S4-style bilinear]
variants.zoh_nodt: Delta = tau*g(u) (ignores dt); exact ZOH formulas   [intentionally grid-dependent toy]
variants.eulerB_nodt: Delta = tau*g(u); Abar = exp(Delta*lambda); Bbar = Delta*B(u)   [Mamba-style discretization recipe in a toy; NOT the Mamba architecture]

model.tau: mean step of the base grid, so *_nodt == *_dt on the base grid when it is uniform

grids.base_secondary: jittered: t_k = k*T/K + U(-0.4,0.4)*T/K for interior k
grids.split: each selected base interval (t_{k-1}, t_k] is divided into m equal sub-intervals and every sub-step receives the SAME held value u_k (physical right-held path unchanged)
grids.refine_newobs: each selected base interval is divided into m equal sub-intervals and each new sub-time s receives a NEW observation u(s) from the continuous path (grids nested; base observations unchanged)
grids.mask_nonuniform: only base intervals in the first half of [0,T]

input_path: u(t) = sum_{j=1..3} a_j sin(omega_j t + phi_j), a_j ~ U(0.3,1.0), omega_j ~ U(0.5,3.0), phi_j ~ U(0,2pi)

references.ct_held: RK4 on the continuous-time model driven by the right-held piecewise-constant path of a grid, 64 RK4 sub-steps per grid interval (independent of the ZOH code)
references.ct_true: RK4 on the continuous-time model driven by the true continuous u(t), 512 RK4 sub-steps per base interval; time integrals by composite Simpson

readouts.time_exact: (1/T) * exact integral of the model's intra-step continuous output under the hold (defined only for zoh_* variants; NOT_APPLICABLE otherwise)
readouts.normalization: scale-normalized change = |r_m - r_1| / (rms(y at base times, m=1) * (K_1 if sample_sum else 1))

experiments.FR-E1-SPLIT: uniform split of all base intervals, held input; compare states/outputs at common base times
experiments.FR-E2-NEWOBS: uniform nested refinement with new observations; decompose total change = path_change + (artifact_m - artifact_1)
experiments.FR-E3-READOUT: readouts under (a) nonuniform split and (b) nonuniform new observations
experiments.FR-E4-NUMERICS: failure cases: expm1 vs naive cancellation; bilinear on stiff modes; Euler-B on coarse steps; float32-emulated composition drift

metrics.primary_E1: rel_l2(y at common base times, grid m vs m=1), per unit; aggregate median/max
metrics.primary_E2: artifact_m = rel_l2(y_D(G_m), y_CTheld(G_m)) at common base times

hypotheses.H1: FR-E1 zoh_dt: max over units and m in {2,4,8} of rel_l2(y_m, y_1) <= 1e-12 (float64). Engineering check of a known identity.
hypotheses.H2: FR-E1 eulerB_dt: artifact vs exact held solution decreases with median log-log slope in [-1.2, -0.8].
hypotheses.H3: FR-E1 bilinear_dt: artifact decreases with median log-log slope in [-2.2, -1.8].
hypotheses.H4: FR-E1 zoh_nodt and eulerB_nodt: artifact at m=8 >= artifact at m=2 for >= 90% of units, and median artifact at m=8 >= 0.1.
hypotheses.H5: FR-E2 zoh_dt: artifact_m <= 1e-8 for all units and m; error to ct_true has median slope in [-1.2, -0.8].
hypotheses.H6: FR-E2 zoh_nodt and eulerB_nodt: median artifact at m=8 >= 0.1.
hypotheses.H7: FR-E3(a) zoh_dt: time_exact change <= 1e-12 for all units; median sample_sum and sample_mean change >= 1e-2; time_riemann change > 0 and decreasing in m (median slope < 0).
hypotheses.H8: FR-E3(b) zoh_dt: median error-to-truth of sample_mean at m=8 >= 5 x median error-to-truth of time_exact at m=8.

stop_conditions.S1_bug: If H1 or H5-artifact fails, treat as implementation bug: stop interpretation, debug, log the failure; do not tune thresholds.
stop_conditions.S2_research: If the simple time-handling fix (zoh_dt + time_exact readout) removes the splitting artifact to numerical precision AND the new-observation artifact to reference precision, then this toy provides NO support for a new-architecture claim; record ARCHITECTURE_CLAIM=NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_TOY.
stop_conditions.S3_no_sweep: No parameter sweep beyond this file. No reruns to change outcomes.
